title: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH)
everyday_terms: heart attack at a young age
summary: Familial hypercholesterolaemia means the body cannot clear 'bad' LDL cholesterol from the blood well, so levels are high from birth. Over time this raises the chance of heart disease at a younger age.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal dominant way: one changed copy of one of the genes linked to it (most often LDLR) can be enough to cause it. A parent with the change can pass it on, and the chance is the same for each pregnancy. A genetic counsellor talks this through with you.
carrier_meaning: For a dominant condition, one changed copy can be enough to cause it, so people with a change are not usually called carriers. How much it affects someone varies, and some people have few signs for many years. A genetic counsellor explains what a result means.
disease_meaning: FH is common and very treatable. Finding it early, then care from a doctor with healthy habits and cholesterol-lowering treatment, greatly lowers the chance of heart problems. Close relatives can be offered a cholesterol test.
screening: A simple blood test measures cholesterol, and a genetic test can look for a change in the genes linked to FH. A genetic counsellor can explain which relatives might choose to be tested.

carrier_short: One changed copy. Can be enough to cause the condition. A counsellor explains.
disease_short: High cholesterol from birth; very treatable when found early.
care: Lipid and heart clinics, family doctors, genetic counselling and family support groups.
